title: Edge-label quotient as characters of integral graph cycles
statement:
Let $V,E$ be finite sets with functions $s,t:E\to V$ such that $s(e)\ne t(e)$ for every $e$. Parallel edges are allowed, and neither nonemptiness nor connectedness is assumed. Write $\mathbf Z^S$ for the free $\mathbf Z$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] of functions $S\to\mathbf Z$ for a finite set $S$. Let $\partial:\mathbf Z^E\to\mathbf Z^V$ send the standard basis vector $e$ to $t(e)-s(e)$, and put $H=\ker\partial$. Let $A$ be any commutative group, written multiplicatively. Define $\delta:A^V\to A^E$ by $\delta(a)_e=a_{t(e)}a_{s(e)}^{-1}$ and let $A^E/\operatorname{im}\delta$ denote the quotient group by its image. Evaluation induces a group isomorphism
$$\Phi:A^E/\operatorname{im}\delta\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(H,A),\qquad \Phi([z])(h)=\prod_{e\in E}z_e^{h_e}.$$
Here the Hom group consists of maps from the additive group $H$ to $A$ taking sums to products, with pointwise multiplication. For permutations $\sigma_V,\sigma_E$ preserving the unordered endpoint pairs, let $\epsilon_e=1$ when $s(\sigma_Ee)=\sigma_Vs(e)$ and $\epsilon_e=-1$ otherwise. The signed edge map $\sigma_*$ sends $e$ to $\epsilon_e\sigma_Ee$ and preserves $H$. For $(\sigma^*z)_e=z_{\sigma_Ee}^{\epsilon_e}$ one has
$$\Phi([\sigma^*z])=\Phi([z])\circ\sigma_*.$$
These formulas also identify different choices of orientation by inversion of exactly the reversed edge coordinates.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-graph-incidence-inner-inverse] to choose $r$ with $\partial r\partial=\partial$. Put $p=1-r\partial$. Then $\partial p=0$, and $p(h)=h$ for $h\in H$; thus $p:\mathbf Z^E\to H$ is a linear retraction. No condition on $A$ is used here.

source.place: Agent-written integral-lattice auxiliary for Tag 0C1M, lemma-glue-points, units-sequence proof. The source motivates the edge/vertex quotient but does not assert this graph incidence splitting lemma.

proof.text: For $z\in A^E$ put $L_z(x)=\prod_e z_e^{x_e}$. Integer exponent laws and commutativity give $L_z(x+y)=L_z(x)L_z(y)$ and $L_{zz\prime}=L_zL_{z\prime}$. Moreover $L_{\delta(a)}(h)=\prod_v a_v^{(\partial h)_v}=1$ for $h\in H$. Consequently restriction $L_z|_H$ is constant on cosets of $\operatorname{im}\delta$ and defines the stated homomorphism $\Phi$.

source.place: Agent-written integral-lattice auxiliary for Tag 0C1M, lemma-glue-points, units-sequence proof. The source motivates the edge/vertex quotient but does not assert this graph incidence splitting lemma.

proof.text: Given a character $\chi:H\to A$, use the retraction obtained from [lem-sfb-finite-graph-incidence-inner-inverse] and set $z_e=\chi(p(b_e))$. Expanding $x=\sum_e x_e b_e$ gives $L_z(x)=\chi(p(x))$. For $h\in H$, $p(h)=h$, so $\Phi([z])=\chi$. This proves surjectivity without assuming that $A$ is divisible.

source.place: Agent-written integral-lattice auxiliary for Tag 0C1M, lemma-glue-points, units-sequence proof. The source motivates the edge/vertex quotient but does not assert this graph incidence splitting lemma.

proof.text: If $L_z|_H=1$, then $x=p(x)+r\partial x$ gives $L_z(x)=L_z(r\partial x)$. Define $a_v=L_z(r(b_v))$, using [lem-sfb-finite-graph-incidence-inner-inverse]. For each edge, $\delta(a)_e=L_z(r(b_{t(e)}-b_{s(e)}))=L_z(b_e)=z_e$. Hence the kernel consists exactly of vertex coboundaries. If two cosets have equal characters, apply this calculation to their coordinatewise ratio to see that the cosets agree. Together with the previous step this proves that $\Phi$ is a group isomorphism.

source.place: Agent-written integral-lattice auxiliary for Tag 0C1M, lemma-glue-points, units-sequence proof. The source motivates the edge/vertex quotient but does not assert this graph incidence splitting lemma.

proof.text: Let $S_V(b_v)=b_{\sigma_Vv}$ and $S_E(b_e)=\epsilon_e b_{\sigma_Ee}$. Endpoint preservation gives $\partial S_E(b_e)=\epsilon_e(b_{t(\sigma_Ee)}-b_{s(\sigma_Ee)})=S_V\partial(b_e)$ in both sign cases. Thus $S_E$ preserves $H$. Also $\sigma^*\delta(a)=\delta(a\circ\sigma_V)$ coordinatewise, so $\sigma^*$ descends to the quotient. For $h\in H$, $L_{\sigma^*z}(h)=\prod_e z_{\sigma_Ee}^{\epsilon_e h_e}=L_z(S_Eh)$, proving the required equivariance.

proof.text: For another orientation put $\eta_e=-1$ on reversed edges and $1$ on the others. The map $J$ from its edge lattice to the old one, $J(b_e)=\eta_e b_e$, satisfies $\partial_{\rm old}J=\partial_{\rm new}$. The coordinate map $z\mapsto(z_e^{\eta_e})_e$ takes old coboundaries to new ones and has inverse itself. Evaluation satisfies $L_{(z_e^{\eta_e})}(h)=L_z(Jh)$, which gives exactly the asserted orientation identification.
